{{Short description|A subgroup of a group}}
In [[mathematics]], in the area of [[abstract algebra]] known as [[group theory]], a '''verbal subgroup''' is a [[subgroup]] of a [[group (mathematics)|group]] that is [[Generating set of a group|generated]] by all elements that can be formed by substituting group elements for variables in a given set of [[word (group theory)|words]]. For example, given the word <math>x^2</math>, the corresponding verbal subgroup is the group generated by all squares.

== Examples ==
For a given group <math>G</math> the following are examples of verbal subgroups:
* The entire group <math>G</math>, given by the word <math>x</math>.
* The [[trivial subgroup]], given by the empty word.
* The [[commutator subgroup]], given by the word <math>[x,y]=xyx^{-1}y^{-1}</math>.
** Furthermore every subgroup in the [[derived series]] is a verbal subgroup. The <math>n</math>th term of the derived series <math>G^{(n)}</math> is given by the set of words <math>\{[w,v]\mid w,v\in F^{(n-1)}\}</math> where <math>F</math> is a free group with at least as many generators as <math>G</math>.
** Every subgroup in the [[lower central series]] is a verbal subgroup. The <math>n</math>th term of the lower central series <math>G_{n}</math> is given by the set of words <math>\{[w,x]\mid w\in F_{n-1}\}</math> where <math>F</math> is a free group with at least as many generators as <math>G</math>.

== Properties ==

* Verbal subgroups are [[fully characteristic subgroup]]s.<ref name=Neumann608>{{harv|Neumann|1967|p=608}}</ref><ref name=MKS75>{{harv|Magnus|Karrass|Solitar|2004|p=75}}</ref> That is they are closed under endomorphisms of the ambient group. Since all fully characteristic subgroups are [[normal subgroup]]s, verbal subgroups are normal.
* In free groups, the verbal subgroups are exactly the fully characteristic subgroups.<ref name=Neumann608/> Therefore verbal subgroups represent the generic example of fully characteristic subgroups.<ref name=MKS75/>
* The [[Lattice (order)|lattice]] of verbal subgroups of the countably generated free group under inclusion is [[anti-isomorphism|anti-isomomorphic]] to the lattice of [[Variety (universal algebra)|group varieties]] under inclusion.<ref name=Neumann608/>
